chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Zurara ibn Ayan, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) say:
Indeed, we, the Ahl al-Bayt, our chivalry is the forgiveness of those who wrong us.

key_terms.أهل بيت: Ahl al-Bayt: the Prophet's household, specifically the fourteen infallibles in Shia tradition
key_terms.العفو: Al-'Afw: forgiveness, pardoning — one of God's attributes (al-'Afuww) that the Ahl al-Bayt embody
key_terms.مروءة: Muruwwa: chivalry, magnanimity, noble character — a pre-Islamic Arabian virtue that Islam elevated to mean generosity of spirit

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Sadiq say about the Ahl al-Bayt and forgiveness?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines the distinctive noble character (muruwwa) of the Prophet's household as forgiving those who oppress them. This teaching, delivered in the Imam's circle of trusted companions including Zurara ibn Ayan, reflects the Ahl al-Bayt's spiritual station where forgiveness is not merely a moral recommendation but their defining virtue and noble identity.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. `Ali Majiluwayh narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Ibrahim narrated to us from his father from Hammad b. `Isa from Hariz b. `Abdullah from Zurara b. A`yan. He said: I heard Aba `Abdillah al-Sadiq (as) say:
Surely, our chivalry – the Ahl al-Bayt – is the forgiveness of those who wrong us.
